```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```
```{r}
install.packages("GGally")      # 
install.packages("corrplot")
```

```{r}
library(corrplot)
```



```{r}
library(readr)
INTEGRATED_DATA <- read_csv("INTEGRATED_DATA.csv")
View(INTEGRATED_DATA)
```


```{r}
# Create a visualization of educational attainment
education_data <- INTEGRATED_DATA %>%
  select(PCT_LESS_THAN_HS_15_19, PCT_HS_ONLY_15_19, 
         PCT_SOME_COLLEGE_15_19, PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19) %>%
  gather(key = "Education_Level", value = "Percentage")

ggplot(education_data, aes(x = Percentage, fill = Education_Level)) +
  geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, position = "identity", bins = 20) +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Educational Attainment Across US Counties",
       x = "Percentage of Population", y = "Number of Counties") +
  theme_minimal()

```


```{r}
# install.packages("ggridges") # if not installed
library(ggridges)

ggplot(education_data, aes(x = Percentage, y = Education_Level, fill = Education_Level)) +
  geom_density_ridges(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title = "Ridgeline Plot of Educational Attainment Across US Counties",
       x = "Percentage of Population", y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```


```{r}
ggplot(INTEGRATED_DATA, aes(x = PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19, y = PCTPOVALL_2019, color = WINNING_PARTY)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Relationship Between Bachelor's Degree Attainment and Poverty Rates",
       x = "Percentage with Bachelor's Degree or Higher",
       y = "Poverty Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()


```

```{r}
ggplot(INTEGRATED_DATA, aes(x = WINNING_PARTY, y = UNWMPLOYMENT_RATE, fill = WINNING_PARTY)) +

  labs(title = "Unemployment Rates by Winning Political Party",
```


```{r}
numeric_data <- INTEGRATED_DATA %>%
  select(PCT_LESS_THAN_HS_15_19, PCT_HS_ONLY_15_19, PCT_SOME_COLLEGE_15_19,
         PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19, UNWMPLOYMENT_RATE, PCTPOVALL_2019, TOTAL_VOTES)
# Pairwise scatterplot matrix
#ggpairs(numeric_data)
pairs(numeric_data)
# Correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")
corrplot(cor_matrix, method = "color", type = "upper", tl.cex = 0.8)
```
```{r}
cor_matrix <- cor(numeric_data, use = "complete.obs")

# Base R heatmap
heatmap(cor_matrix,
        main = "Correlation Heatmap",
        col = colorRampPalette(c("blue", "white", "red"))(100),
        scale = "none")
```

```{r}

library(GGally)
library(dplyr)

# Select key numerical variables
numerical_vars <- INTEGRATED_DATA %>% 
  select(PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19, PCTPOVALL_2019, UNWMPLOYMENT_RATE, TOTAL_VOTES)

# Create pairwise plot
ggpairs(numerical_vars,
        title = "Pairwise Comparison of Key Numerical Variables",
        upper = list(continuous = "cor"),  # Show correlation in upper triangle
        lower = list(continuous = "points"), # Scatterplots in lower triangle
        diag = list(continuous = "barDiag")) # Histograms on diagonal
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)  # needed for rownames_to_column

# Select key numerical variables
numerical_vars <- INTEGRATED_DATA %>% 
  select(PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19, PCTPOVALL_2019, UNWMPLOYMENT_RATE, TOTAL_VOTES)

# Compute correlation matrix
cor_matrix <- cor(numerical_vars, use = "complete.obs")

# Convert correlation matrix to long format
cor_long <- as.data.frame(cor_matrix) %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "Var1") %>%
  pivot_longer(-Var1, names_to = "Var2", values_to = "Correlation")

# Plot heatmap
ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = Var1, y = Var2, fill = Correlation)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Correlation, 2)), size = 4) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", midpoint = 0,
                       limit = c(-1,1), name = "Correlation") +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Pairwise Relationships Between Key Variables", x = "", y = "")
```

```{r}
ggplot(INTEGRATED_DATA, aes(x = PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19, y = PCTPOVALL_2019, color = WINNING_PARTY)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Bachelor's Degree vs Poverty Rate by Party",
       x = "Percentage with Bachelor's Degree or Higher",
       y = "Poverty Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
ggplot(INTEGRATED_DATA, aes(x = WINNING_PARTY, y = UNWMPLOYMENT_RATE, fill = WINNING_PARTY)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red")) +
  labs(title = "Unemployment Rate by Winning Party",
       x = "Winning Party", y = "Unemployment Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()

# Violin plot
ggplot(INTEGRATED_DATA, aes(x = WINNING_PARTY, y = PCTPOVALL_2019, fill = WINNING_PARTY)) +
  geom_violin(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red")) +
  labs(title = "Poverty Rate Distribution by Party",
       x = "Winning Party", y = "Poverty Rate (%)") +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
ggplot(INTEGRATED_DATA, aes(x = PCT_BAC_0R_HIGH_15_19, y = PCTPOVALL_2019, 
                 size = TOTAL_VOTES, color = WINNING_PARTY)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.6) +
  scale_size(range = c(1, 10)) +
  labs(title = "Education vs Poverty with Total Votes",
       x = "Percentage with Bachelor's Degree or Higher",
       y = "Poverty Rate (%)",
       size = "Total Votes") +
  theme_minimal()
```
